focus: P6 TransitionRefusalV1 stable schema, authority boundary, typed detail, observations, prerequisites, retryability, evidence, causality, and non-authorizing suggestions
noveltyJustification: Repo 1 and iteration 009 established typed denials and zero domain mutation; this iteration adds stable wire identity, boundary/disposition separation, a closed detail union, three-time observations, code-owned recovery classes, non-authorizing prerequisite/action contracts, and causal/evidence rules across compile, claim, budget, gate, belief, policy, fence, and effect failures.
keyFindings: TransitionRefusalV1 is a typed response over a failed attempt; only the referenced gateway decision or commit guard enforces denial, and the refusal never authorizes
Stable schema, code/version, refusal digest, attempted-transition identity, authority epoch, and policy identity are independent and machine-readable
Clients branch on a closed detail union and code-owned registry, never prose or LLM parsing
Expected, boundary-observed, and optional response-current head, state, version, claim, authority, and fence facts remain distinct
Retry is a conditional class requiring refresh, prerequisite, resource, policy, operator, idempotent-success, or effect-recovery semantics
Prerequisites and suggestions are advisory typed data requiring a new authorized request and carry no commands, tokens, leases, or capabilities
Evidence references and correlation/causation support replay and explanation without proving authorization

ruledOut.approach: Represent refusal as a domain event or authorization proof
ruledOut.reason: The gateway decision or commit guard rejects the attempt; the response has zero domain/effect authority

ruledOut.approach: Use reason or suggestion prose as client protocol
ruledOut.reason: Presentation can change and unknown semantics must fail closed; clients select on versioned discriminants
Safe recovery differs across stale head, fence, budget, gate, belief, policy, already-applied, and in-doubt effects

ruledOut.approach: Treat observed current head or fence as a reusable grant
ruledOut.reason: It is one boundary observation and may be stale at delivery; a new request must re-enter checks

ruledOut.approach: Embed executable recovery commands or capability material
ruledOut.reason: Advice forms a future request and never bypasses authorization, claim, fence, gate, budget, belief, or effect recovery

nextFocus: P6 recovery semantics across compile claim budget gate and belief failures
